request: We've built a reporting add-on for our existing B2B product and want a go-to-market plan for selling it into a customer segment we've never targeted before.

objective.value: Win first customers for the reporting add-on in a new, never-targeted customer segment. The specific outcome (number of customers, revenue, pipeline) and the date are not stated.
objective.evidence: Client: 'go-to-market plan for selling it into a customer segment we've never targeted before.'

success_metric.evidence: No leading indicator or counting rule stated.

icp.value: Unknown segment. Only known: it is new to the company, and the buyer is a business (B2B). Segment, buyer role and size are unspecified.
icp.evidence: Client: 'a customer segment we've never targeted before.'

existing_distribution.value: The company has an existing B2B product with a customer base, which is probably usable for upsell or referrals. Nothing is known about reach into the new segment: lists, partners, community, brand.
existing_distribution.evidence: Client: 'our existing B2B product'; 'never targeted' suggests little or no direct presence in the segment.

offer.value: A reporting add-on to the existing B2B product. Pricing, packaging, trial terms, and whether it is sold standalone or only to existing-product users are unknown.
offer.evidence: Client: 'We've built a reporting add-on for our existing B2B product.'

objections.value: Unknown. Likely: the new segment must adopt the base product to use the add-on, plus data handling and trust for financial or operational data. This is unconfirmed.
objections.evidence: The add-on depends on the existing product, so it moves the buyer's data and workflow. No objection is stated.

alternatives.value: Unknown what the new segment uses for reporting today (spreadsheets, BI tools, a competitor, an in-house build) or what that costs. Impact is raised because the offer will be priced.

channels.value: No channels identified. Impact is raised because there is no known distribution into the segment, and the segment may be regulated.
channels.evidence: No channels named. The segment is new, so existing distribution may not carry over.

unit_economics.evidence: No price, margin, CAC tolerance or lifetime value stated.

capacity.value: Unknown: people and hours per week available for go-to-market, and for how many weeks. This is the binding constraint.

horizon.evidence: No date or review point stated.

decision_thresholds.evidence: Not stated. They depend on the objective, horizon and economics.

questions.q: Which segment is it, and what does the add-on do for them? Please name the segment (industry, company size, buyer role) and say who in that segment you would NOT sell to.
questions.why: High uncertainty × high impact: every other choice (channels, message, price, regulation) follows from the segment, and it is currently unknown.

questions.q: How many people can work on this, for how many hours per week and for how many weeks? Is any of that already taken by other work?
questions.why: High uncertainty × high impact: a plan that does not fit the hours available is not a plan, whatever the budget says.

questions.q: What do you already have in or near this segment: customers who sit in it or know people in it, a mailing list, partners or resellers, a community or a following? Or is it a cold start?
questions.why: High uncertainty × high impact: existing reach decides which channels are viable at all, so it comes before any new channel.

questions.q: Must a buyer in the new segment already use your core product, or can the add-on be sold on its own? How do you plan to price it, and is there a price in mind?
questions.why: High impact: this decides whether the sale involves adopting two products or one, and it sets the objection and the price anchor.

questions.q: What is the outcome you want and by when (for example, N paying customers or a revenue figure in a given number of months), and what early signal would tell you it's working or not?
questions.why: High uncertainty × high impact: without a target and a clock, thresholds to continue, change or stop cannot be set.

questions.q: What does this segment use for reporting today, and what do you expect to be the main reason they would not switch to or buy yours?
questions.why: The offer will be priced, so positioning and the price anchor are defined against the current alternative. The objection often decides conversion.

summary.objective: Win the first paying customers for the reporting add-on in a customer segment the company has never sold to. Target and deadline are not yet defined.
summary.scope: A go-to-market plan: segment definition, positioning against current alternatives, offer and pricing, channels sized to the available capacity, and measurable thresholds for deciding to continue, change or stop.
assumptions: The add-on depends on the existing product, so new-segment buyers may need to adopt it first.
Existing distribution probably does not carry over to the new segment.
Reporting involves sensitive business data, so trust and data handling are likely objections.
summary.blind_spot: The hours actually available for go-to-market work, and what reach the company already has into the new segment. Together they decide which channels are viable at all, and no plan can be sized until they are known.

objective.value: Win first customers for the reporting add-on in a new customer segment the company has never targeted. No target outcome (number of customers, revenue) or date stated.

objections.value: Unknown. Impact raised because a reporting add-on moves the buyer's data into the product (data handling, trust, reconciliation with their own figures) and a new segment has no prior trust in the vendor.
objections.evidence: Nothing stated. Impact raised from the data-movement signal.

alternatives.value: Unknown what the segment uses today (spreadsheets, BI tools, a competitor, an accountant). Impact raised because the add-on will be priced and the pitch is defined against it.

channels.value: No candidate routes stated. Impact raised because there is no known distribution in the segment, and the segment may be regulated or carry outreach rules (cold-contact law).

capacity.value: Unknown: people and hours per week available for sales and marketing, and for how many weeks. 'We' suggests a team, not a solo builder.
capacity.evidence: Client says "we"; no hours or headcount given.

horizon.evidence: No date or review point stated.

instrumentation.evidence: Nothing stated. Low impact until a metric is chosen.

decision_thresholds.evidence: No continue / change / stop rule stated.

questions.q: Which segment is it, and who inside it would buy (role, company size, sector)? And can you name a type of company in that segment that it is NOT for?
questions.why: uncertainty × impact: everything else (channels, price, pitch, objections) depends on it, and it is currently unknown. A regulated sector would also change channels and offer.

questions.q: How many people, and roughly how many hours per week, can go into selling this over the next few months? Is that time already committed, or does it compete with other work?
questions.why: uncertainty × impact: the binding constraint. A plan that needs more hands than exist is not a plan, whatever the budget.

questions.q: What do you already have in this new segment: customers who resemble it, a mailing list, a community, a partner, or personal contacts? Or is it a cold start?
questions.why: uncertainty × impact: this decides which channels are even viable, and should be settled before designing any new one.

questions.q: Would someone in the new segment buy the add-on on its own, or must they first adopt your core product? And what do they use for reporting today?
questions.why: uncertainty × impact: standalone vs. bundled is a different sales motion and price, and the current tool defines the price anchor and the pitch.

questions.q: What would make this a success, and by when (for example, a number of paying customers or a revenue figure by a given date)? Is there a budget, and is it fixed or released only if early results are good?
questions.why: uncertainty × impact: without a target and a clock there is nothing to measure the plan against or to set stop/continue thresholds on.

summary.objective: Launch a go-to-market for the already-built reporting add-on to win first customers in a segment the company has never sold to. Target, date and success measure are not yet defined.
summary.scope: A go-to-market plan: who to target in the new segment, the offer and price, the channels, and the checkpoints that tell you whether to continue, change or stop. The product build is out of scope (the add-on already exists).
assumptions: The segment is new, so the existing customer base and audience probably do not match it (inferred, unconfirmed).
The add-on is sold as an extension of the existing B2B product; whether it can be bought standalone is unknown.
'We' implies a small team rather than a solo builder; hours available are unknown.
Demand and willingness to pay in the new segment are untested and will most likely need a small, cheap test rather than more discussion.
summary.blind_spot: The segment is unnamed and there is no known distribution into it, so channels, price and pitch cannot be designed yet. Together with the unknown time available, a plan could easily assume more reach and more hours than exist.

summary.objective: Sell the existing reporting add-on into a customer segment the company has never targeted. The target outcome and deadline are not yet defined.
summary.scope: A go-to-market plan for the new segment: who exactly it is, what is offered and at what price, how to reach them given what already exists, how to measure it, and when to continue or stop. Nothing beyond the one-line request is known yet.
assumptions: The company has no meaningful existing audience in the new segment (inferred from 'never targeted before').
The add-on is sold on top of the existing B2B product, so the buyer may need the core product (to confirm).
The offer is priced, so the buyer's current alternatives will set the price anchor.
The add-on works with the buyer's own data, so data handling and switching effort are likely objections.
summary.blind_spot: The human time actually available for go-to-market work. Together with whether any existing relationship reaches the new segment, this decides which channels are realistic. A plan that assumes more hands, or more audience, than exist will not be executed.
